title: Artifact provenance verification and encumbered-weights resolution for model onboarding
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Background: As external model ingestion volume grows, we need a deterministic, auditable gate that (1) detects encumbered or otherwise restricted weight artifacts, (2) verifies provenance signatures/hashes, and (3) prevents publishing performance profiles or allowing public catalog use until mitigations/approvals are complete. Current intake is manual and inconsistent across legal, research, and product teams, which results in blocked uploads, surprise compliance work, and accidental exposure of restricted models.

Goal: Deliver an automated provenance + license risk pipeline integrated into the onboarding UI and the model catalog ingestion API that outputs a machine-readable risk score and a human-facing review checklist. Models scoring above the automated-block threshold should surface a mandatory review flow with legal/partner-solution onboarding and prevent performance profile publication and default routing into hosted inference until cleared.

Scope (MVP):
- Automated artifact checks at upload time: compute SHA512 of weight bundles, extract/validate provided provenance.json (if present), and verify detached signatures (supporting simple sigs and sigstore-style attestation).
- License parsing: attempt SPDX extraction from repository metadata and from manifest files inside the artifact; fall back to ML-assisted license classification for ambiguous cases.
- Restricted-weights detector: heuristic ruleset + allowlist/denylist (e.g., encumbered commercial checkpoints, known proprietary checkpoints). Flags: ENCUMBERED_WEIGHTS, UNKNOWN_SOURCE, LICENSE_CONFLICT.
- Risk scoring: combine license restrictiveness, signature provenance confidence, and source reputation into a 0-100 risk score. Risk score >= 75 triggers auto-block, 50-74 places it in expedited review queue, <50 auto-approve (non-blocking).
- Console surface: show "Risk score", primary flags, signature hash, and links to artifacts, plus CTA to request legal review. Block publish button for models >= 75.
- Performance profile publishing: block automatic performance profile publish and public catalog listing until model moves to Cleared state.
- Audit log: append immutable audit entry with computed hash, scanner version, and decision for every onboarding attempt.

Acceptance criteria:
- Onboarded model with an open-source license (e.g., Apache-2.0, MIT) + validated signature => risk score < 50 and allowed to publish performance profile automatically.
- Model bundle with missing provenance but public source URL that matches a known mirror yields a reproducible hash and risk score between 50-74 and creates expedited-review task.
- Artifact containing weights with known restricted provenance (denylist) triggers ENCUMBERED_WEIGHTS flag and sets status to Blocked; console prevents making model public and blocks performance profile publish.
- Every onboarding event is surfaced in Console timeline and recorded in system audit logs with hash and scanner version.

Implementation notes / proposed design decisions:
- Scanner as an idempotent microservice (scanner-v1) invoked synchronously during upload for fast feedback. For very large files, compute hash in background but create a provisional Risk Score using manifest metadata and re-evaluate when full hash is available.
- Use SPDX parsing library + fallback to an internal lightweight license classifier trained to detect vendor-proprietary vs permissive licenses. Classifier outputs probable license text + confidence.
- Maintain a central "Restricted Weights Registry" (RWR) that is a curated denylist + allowlist. RWR is editable by SRE/Legal via Console with strict audit trail.
- Implement attestations: accept signed provenance blobs (JSON) with optional certificate chains. Integrate sigstore-style verification later in rollout plan.
- Version pinning: when a model passes onboarding, the system must record the exact artifact hash and expose a pin for serving (customers can only select pinned artifact hashes for production routing unless they opt into floating channels with explicit notice).

UX & API requirements:
- Console: new onboarding flow step "Provenance & Licensing" with inline risk breakdown and explicit "Request Legal Review" button. Prevent "Publish profile" and "Make public" actions when model state == Blocked.
- API: onboarding endpoint returns structured fields: ["risk_score", "flags", "artifact_hash", "scanner_version", "review_task_id"]. These must be strings or lists in the API response for easy ingestion by downstream automation (note: API design doc linked).

Operational/Runbook items:
- Maintain scanner versioning; releases of scanner must include changelog and migration notes; each audit entry must record scanner_version.
- Define SLA for expedited reviews: 72 hours for Risk 50-74; 5 business days for high-risk manual review unless escalated.
- Monitoring: percent of blocked uploads, average review time, false-positive rates (measured by manual overturns), and customer complaints.

Risks & open questions:
- ML license classifier false positives for non-English license text — mitigation: fall back to manual review if classifier confidence < 0.6.
- Large artifacts cause upload latency — mitigation: provisional acceptance with background verification and UI messaging about "final verification pending".
- Edge cases where customers intentionally upload obfuscated weights — may require escalated legal review and possible refusal to onboard.

Links & artifacts:
- Confluence: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/INF/pages/Onboarding+Provenance+Playbook
- Prototype UI mockups: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1abcMockupsOnboarding
- Schema PR (API): https://github.com/redwood-inference/catalog/pull/402
- Scanner prototype repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/provenance-scanner (WIP)

Next steps & short-term plan (next 3 sprints):
1) Engineering: implement scanner-v1 minimal checks + hash computation (Sprint 1)
2) Product/Design: finalize Console mockups and error states for "Blocked"/"Awaiting verification" (Sprint 1)
3) Legal: define initial allowlist/denylist seeds and review thresholds (Sprint 2)
4) Engineering: integrate scanner into onboarding API and block publication flows; persist audit entries (Sprint 2)
5) Pilot: invite two existing partners to trial onboarding flow and collect feedback (Sprint 3)

Owner: PM + Eng + Legal triage. This ticket coordinates cross-functional work; subsequent engineering subtasks should be created under ENG-xxx and linked as children.
